# Indriyakathā (Kv 19.8)

**ID:** Kv 19.8
**Section:** Kathāvatthu (kv)
**Collection:** Abhidhamma
**Title (Pali):** Indriyakathā
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh03m3.mul26.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The text addresses a doctrinal controversy regarding whether spiritual qualities such as confidence (*saddhā*), energy (*viriya*), mindfulness (*sati*), concentration (*samādhi*), and wisdom (*paññā*) can properly be distinguished from their status as "faculties" (*indriya*, such as *saddhindriya*) on the premise that ordinary (*lokiya*) qualities are merely mundane mental factors while the faculties are exclusively supramundane or transcendent (*lokuttara*) [Gethin 2001]. The *Kathāvatthu* rejects this restriction, asserting that it is entirely legitimate to designate mundane confidence and the other four qualities as faculties [Gethin 2001]. According to the *Kathāvatthu* commentary cited by modern scholars, this opposing thesis was upheld by the Hetuvādins and the Mahīśāsakas [Gethin 2001].

  DharmaNexus additionally aligns segments of the text with the Tibetan *Vyutpatti* [DharmaNexus].
